generated_note: Lindos game compatibility matrix — the single source of truth for Lindos Settings → Gaming → Compatibility and for docs/COMPATIBILITY.md (generated by tests/gen-compat-doc.py). Statuses are a snapshot: whether a MULTIPLAYER game runs on Linux is decided by its anti-cheat vendor and the publisher, not by Lindos, and can change with one update. Lindos runs Windows games through Wine/Proton (a translation layer, not Windows). Always double-check protondb.com and areweanticheatyet.com before buying. 'not_possible' = will not run on ANY Linux distribution today, including Lindos.

statuses.native: Developer ships a Linux build (no compatibility layer).
statuses.works: Runs through Proton (Steam/umu/Heroic), Wine (Lutris/Bottles) or a dedicated Linux client; near-native performance.
statuses.partial: Runs with caveats: third-party launcher, unofficial client, unstable, or some modes/features missing.
statuses.not_possible: Blocked by a kernel-level anti-cheat with no Linux build, or the publisher disabled their anti-cheat's Linux support. Nothing on the Lindos side can change this.

entries.reason: Roblox's Windows player blocks Wine (Hyperion anti-cheat), but the community Sober runtime runs the official Android build natively on Linux with the normal Roblox account. Install: lindos-game install sober. Not affiliated with Roblox Corporation.

Roblox Studio (the editor, not the player) runs through Wine via Vinegar (Flatpak org.vinegarhq.Vinegar; lindos-game install vinegar). Works for building/testing places; occasional breakage after Studio updates.

Native Linux Java build. Prism Launcher (lindos-game install prism) manages instances, mods, shaders and bundled Java runtimes; a Microsoft account that owns Minecraft is required. Multiplayer servers work exactly as on Windows.

No official Linux build. The unofficial mcpelauncher (Flatpak io.mrarm.mcpelauncher; lindos-game install mcpelauncher) runs the Android version you own on Google Play. Marketplace and Realms may not work; Mojang does not support it.

Vanguard is a Windows kernel-mode driver with no Linux build and Riot has stated it will not support Linux. Does not run on any Linux distribution, including Lindos — no workaround, and attempts risk the account.
Ran under Wine/Lutris until Riot made Vanguard mandatory in 2024; since then it does not run on any Linux. Same for Teamfight Tactics on PC.

entries.anticheat: Easy Anti-Cheat (BattlEye was removed in June 2024; Linux support stays disabled by Epic)
entries.reason: Both anti-cheats support Proton, but Epic has explicitly chosen not to enable EAC's Linux runtime for its own game and has repeatedly said it will not. Honest routes instead: NVIDIA GeForce NOW's official Linux app (free tier), Xbox Cloud Gaming in Chrome/Edge (free, no Game Pass needed), Boosteroid (EU/NA/BR) or Amazon Luna (not India) — see 'lindos-game route fortnite'.

cloud.note: Own Epic account; play through the native Linux app (not a browser).
Free, up to 1-hour sessions; no Game Pass needed — only a free Microsoft account (with an Xbox profile) and a linked Epic account.
Free in Boosteroid's Library; Europe/North America/Brazil only.
Included in Luna Standard (bundled with Prime); not available in India.

entries.anticheat: Easy Anti-Cheat (Linux support disabled; switching to EA Javelin on 2026-09-29)
entries.reason: Worked on Proton until November 2024, when EA/Respawn disabled Linux and Steam Deck support in the name of anti-cheat. On 2026-09-29 Apex switches its PC anti-cheat to EA Javelin; EA has stated Secure Boot is NOT required for Apex specifically. Launching now fails or results in an error; do not attempt with a valued account. Honest route: NVIDIA GeForce NOW (EA app variant, free tier) — see 'lindos-game route apex'.

cloud.note: EA app variant only (no Steam variant listed). Re-verify after 2026-09-29, when Apex switches to EA Javelin anti-cheat.

entries.reason: Native Linux build from Valve; VAC works. Third-party leagues (FACEIT, ESEA) use their own kernel anti-cheat and are not available on Linux.
Native Linux build from Valve.
Valve's shooter runs through Proton with VAC (no native build yet). Verify current state on ProtonDB — early-access title.

Single-player Story Mode runs well through Proton (Legacy and Enhanced editions). Turn BattlEye off in the Rockstar Games Launcher settings (Rockstar's FAQ describes this for Story-Mode-only play), then start Story Mode. GTA Online is a separate entry below.

entries.anticheat: BattlEye (kernel-level, Linux support not enabled by Rockstar)
entries.reason: Rockstar added BattlEye to GTA Online on 17 September 2024 without enabling its Linux/Proton support; Rockstar's FAQ states Steam Deck/Linux are not supported. Online has not worked since; Story Mode still does. Re-verify on areweanticheatyet.com — this is Rockstar's call, not a Lindos limitation.
Runs through Proton with EAC enabled; co-op/invasions work. Steam Deck Verified. Nightreign works the same way.
Runs through Proton (Steam or GOG via Heroic) including Phantom Liberty; ray tracing/FSR work with recent Mesa/NVIDIA drivers.

The Linux-native build was discontinued in 2020, but the Windows version runs through Proton: Epic version via Heroic, Steam version for existing owners. Cross-play and ranked work; not listed as blocked on areweanticheatyet.com.

Runs through Wine with the third-party 'An Anime Game Launcher' (AAGL) which patches the anti-cheat driver requirement. HoYoverse neither supports nor (so far) bans it, but that can change — use at your own risk. Not available through Steam.

entries.anticheat: BattlEye + FairFight (Linux support not enabled by Ubisoft)
entries.reason: Ubisoft has not enabled BattlEye's Proton support and Siege X's kernel anti-cheat requirements make it worse; the game does not run on any Linux.

cloud.note: Ubisoft Connect and Steam variants both work.
Free Access is cloud-playable with any Game Pass tier once claimed.

entries.anticheat: BattlEye (Linux support not enabled by Bungie)
entries.reason: Bungie explicitly forbids running Destiny 2 through Proton/Wine and threatens bans; the game detects Linux and refuses to start.

cloud.note: Epic and Steam variants both work; requires the owned game.

entries.reason: Krafton uses several anti-cheats without Linux support; the game does not get past the anti-cheat check on Proton.
Runs through Proton on Steam, or via the Battle.net client installed by the Lutris 'Battle.net' script. Blizzard tolerates Wine/Proton. Steam Deck Verified.
Runs through Proton, but the mandatory EA app is fragile under Wine (login loops, updates). Steam version via Proton is the smoothest; Heroic can also install the EA version. Mods work.
Steam version runs through Proton with online play; Steam Deck Verified. The Microsoft Store/Game Pass version is not installable on Linux.
Runs through Proton (Steam Deck Verified). Needs vm.max_map_count raised — Lindos ships /etc/sysctl.d/80-lindos-gaming.conf for exactly this.
343 enabled EAC for Linux in March 2024; multiplayer works with current Proton (use Proton Experimental or GE if a season update breaks it).
Runs through Proton including dedicated/co-op servers; Steam Deck Playable.
GameGuard was enabled for Proton at launch; runs well through Proton (Steam Deck Playable).
NetEase enabled EAC's Linux support at launch; runs through Proton and is Steam Deck Verified.
Digital Extremes officially supports Proton/Steam Deck; the launcher and game update fine.
Runs through Proton (Vulkan renderer recommended); GOG version via Heroic. Steam Deck Verified. Cross-save/multiplayer work.
Native Linux build; SMAPI mods work.
Native Linux build; tModLoader too.
Runs through Proton with cross-play (Steam Deck Verified).

entries.anticheat: Easy Anti-Cheat (Epic Online Services, not officially enabled for Linux)
entries.reason: Epic/Mediatonic do not officially support Linux, but the game currently runs through Proton GE / Proton Experimental (Epic version via Heroic, Steam version for pre-2022 owners). Community-reported as 'Running', can break with any update — verify before relying on it.

entries.anticheat: Easy Anti-Cheat (Linux support refused by Facepunch)
entries.reason: EAC supports Proton, but Facepunch stated (October 2022) they will not enable it for Linux/Steam Deck; the game kicks Linux clients from all official and most community servers.

cloud.note: Needs a paid Performance or Ultimate membership.

entries.anticheat: BattlEye (Linux support not enabled by Battlestate)
entries.reason: The launcher and login can work under Wine, but raids require BattlEye's Linux runtime which Battlestate has not enabled — areweanticheatyet.com lists it as 'Planned', not working. Tarkov 1.0 released on Steam (app 3932890) on 2025-11-15; still not on any cloud service. Treat as not playable until BattlEye-Linux is enabled.

entries.game: Call of Duty (Warzone / Black Ops 6 / Modern Warfare III)
entries.reason: Ricochet is a Windows kernel-mode driver; Activision does not support Linux and bans are reported for attempts. Applies to every current Call of Duty title on Steam and Battle.net.

cloud.note: Steam, Battle.net and Xbox-app/PC-Game-Pass variants all work.
Black Ops 7 needs Game Pass Ultimate, or a purchase to stream on Essential/Premium; Warzone/Black Ops 6/MWIII need any tier.
Steam/Battle.net/Xbox variants; not available in India.

entries.reason: Team Jade's kernel-level anti-cheat has no Linux component and the developers have said Linux/Steam Deck are not supported.
Embark enabled EAC's Linux support at launch; runs through Proton (Steam Deck Playable).
Behaviour enabled EAC for Proton on Steam and Epic (Heroic); Steam Deck Verified.
EA's kernel-level anti-cheat (added 2023) has no Linux build; the game refuses to start under Proton.

cloud.note: Needs Xbox Game Pass Ultimate plus a game purchase.

entries.anticheat: EA Javelin (kernel driver, Secure Boot required)
entries.reason: Javelin is a Windows kernel driver that additionally requires Secure Boot/TPM attestation; EA has stated Linux and Steam Deck are not supported.

cloud.note: Needs a paid Performance or Ultimate membership; EA app and Steam.

entries.reason: Runs through Proton (Vulkan renderer); Steam Deck Playable. Path of Exile 1 works the same way.
Steam version through Proton (Steam Deck Verified) or Battle.net via Lutris.
Battle.net client installs through the Lutris 'Battle.net' script; WoW (Retail and Classic) runs well under Wine/DXVK. Blizzard tolerates Wine.
Rare enabled EAC for Proton; Steam version runs (Steam Deck Playable). Microsoft Store/Game Pass version is not installable on Linux.
Crytek enabled EAC's Linux support in 2023; runs through Proton.
EAC enabled for Proton; runs with occasional launcher quirks (verify ProtonDB after major patches).
Gaijin ships a native Linux client (Steam or standalone launcher).
Amazon enabled EAC for Proton in 2022; runs through Proton (Steam Deck Playable).
Amazon enabled EAC's Linux support; runs through Proton (Steam Deck Playable).
Runs through Wine/Proton with the community LUG helper (Lutris installer). Playable, but heavy: needs vm.max_map_count raised (Lindos ships it) and 16+ GB RAM; every patch can break it. Not on Steam.

Use Heroic (lindos-game install heroic) instead of Epic's own launcher: it downloads, installs and runs Epic/GOG/Amazon titles through Proton. Individual games keep their own anti-cheat status (Fortnite: not possible).
Lutris' Battle.net installer sets up the client under Wine; Overwatch 2, WoW, Diablo, Hearthstone, StarCraft II work. Call of Duty titles do NOT (Ricochet).

Both launchers install through Lutris/Heroic and run under Wine, but they are fragile (login loops, self-updates). Games with EA anticheat/Javelin (Battlefield 2042/6, Apex) or Ubisoft's BattlEye titles (Siege) remain not possible regardless.

The Xbox app and Microsoft Store game installs are Windows-only (UWP packaging, licensing) and cannot be installed under Wine. Xbox Cloud Gaming streaming works in Chrome or Edge (never Firefox; Linux is not officially listed) but needs a Game Pass Essential/Premium/Ultimate subscription — PC Game Pass alone does NOT include cloud gaming. Steam versions of the same games are usually fine.

cloud.note: Needs Game Pass Essential, Premium or Ultimate — PC Game Pass alone does NOT include cloud gaming. Some titles are also on GeForce NOW's XBOX-store variant once you link an Xbox account (e.g. Call of Duty).

geforce-now.name: NVIDIA GeForce NOW
geforce-now.note: Official Linux app (Ubuntu 24.04). The browser client is not supported on Linux. Needs a GPU with Vulkan H.264/H.265 video decode; reinstall the app after changing GPU drivers.

xbox-cloud.name: Xbox Cloud Gaming
xbox-cloud.subscription: Game Pass Essential/Premium/Ultimate (5/10/15 h/month from Nov 2026); NOT included with PC Game Pass; some free-to-play titles (Fortnite) need no Game Pass at all
xbox-cloud.note: Works in Microsoft Edge or Google Chrome on Linux (mouse/keyboard needs fullscreen in one of those two); Linux is not officially listed. Streams the console version, never Firefox.

boosteroid.name: Boosteroid
boosteroid.note: Official Linux .deb/.rpm client (X11; Wayland runs it through XWayland). Available in Europe, North America and Brazil only — not India.

amazon-luna.name: Amazon Luna
amazon-luna.note: Linux is not officially listed (Chrome/Edge only); not available in India. Luna Standard comes bundled with Prime.
